title: Israel's president picks Gadi Eisenkot, not Netanyahu, to try to form a government
dek: After an election with no clear winner, the person who tries first to build a majority is no longer the sitting prime minister. Whether Eisenkot can do it is not settled.
what: On Saturday, 7 November 2026, Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he would ask Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, to form the next government. AP reported it as a setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Times of Israel reports that Herzog told both men of his decision that evening and that the formal handover was set for 5 p.m. on Sunday at the President's Residence. I did not find a report of the ceremony itself.

The Times of Israel and Al Jazeera report that in Herzog's consultations Eisenkot was recommended by 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset and Netanyahu by 46. The seven-member United Torah Judaism faction recommended neither. Under Israeli law Eisenkot has 28 days to build a coalition, and the president can add up to 14 days.

Al Jazeera reports that the election was held on 27 October and that Eisenkot's alliance won 48 seats, Netanyahu's bloc 53 and Arab-led parties 19, with 61 needed for a majority. It reports that Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, although some of them recommended him, so he would need the ultra-Orthodox parties to reach 61. These are the outlet's figures and I checked them only against that report.

Al Jazeera quotes Netanyahu as saying a government "dependent on Islamists" would dismantle the state from within. What happens if Eisenkot fails was described differently in the pages I read, so I leave it out.
why: Israel's president, not the largest bloc, decides who tries first, and this choice goes against the sitting prime minister. Posts about it are spreading mostly as news of Netanyahu's setback.
next: Watch whether the handover takes place on Sunday and which parties join Eisenkot in the 28 days that follow.

sources.label: Al Jazeera: Israel's president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government
Times of Israel: Herzog announces he will task Eisenkot tomorrow with forming new government
